Climate Action Plan (CAP)

Shannon DZ amongst others. https://climateconnected.ie/category/decarbonization-zone/

Community Climate Action Programme (CCAP) Fund  
CCAP Strand 1 Phase 1 & Strand 1a

Strand 1a.

• Some projects may need an extension to this date & Climate Action have been in contact with the 
DCEE on that.  Extensions will be permissible, but groups must now give a realistic completion date.  
There will be no extension dates permitted past the end of April. 
• Climate Action will liaise with affected groups to support successful completion of projects, grant 
payout and drawdown. 
CCAP Strand 1 Phase 2 
• Applications for CCAP Strand 1 Phase 2 closed on 16 December 2025.   
• 29 applications received from community groups across the county with funding sought totalling 
approximately €1.16 million versus an available fund of €300,000.   
• The local level evaluation process for completed applications will be completed by early February 
with Department (DCEE) evaluation completed by early April with letters of offer issued soon after.

COMMUNITY AND INTERGATION 
Local Enhancement Programme 2025 
On 13th June 2025, the Department of Rural and Community Development and an Gaeltacht announced 
€114,782.86 for 148 projects in Co Leitrim under the Local Enhancement Programme 2025. All payments 
have been made under the Current and Capital stream and redistribution of funds has been approved 
and paid out. Preparation of final report to Department commenced with submission due in January. 
 
Age Friendly Programme   
January date confirmed for delivery of the Age Friendly Business programme in Carrick on Shannon, 
location Carrick Campus. The end of year reporting submitted to Age Friendly Ireland and preparation of 
2026 plans commenced. Age Friendly content was delivered as part of the ‘Stay Safe Stay Well’ winter 
ready events which were delivered in Ballinamore and Mohill. 
Healthy Ireland 
Healthy Leitrim attended the Healthy Ireland Local Government 2026 Planning Conference in Wexford on 
December 2nd and 3rd. Healthy Leitrim presented on physical and mental resilience in Mohill on 
December 5th as part of Leitrim County Councils Stay Safe, Stay Well workshop series. Healthy Leitrim 
continues to work with Mohill FSC to identify a coordinator to reinvigorate and relaunch the ‘We’re 
Breastfeeding Friendly Leitrim’ campaign across businesses in the County with a work plan being 
devised in collaboration with peer support groups and other collaborators being sought including 
Carrick Chamber of Commerce and the Local Enterprise Office.  
A selection of baby friendly toys have now been provided to each of 4 libraries as we continue to work in 
collaboration with Rory & Caroline and the ‘Healthy Ireland in your Library’ project to identify baby 
friendly opportunities within libraries including access to peer support groups for parents (Dromahair 
Library, Mohill Library and Ballinamore Library), introduction of a series of breastfeeding books, and 
opportunities for pregnant, postpartum and new parents to avail of services including talks from health 
care professionals, baby massage programmes, dads to be masterclasses and pediatric first aid. 
 
Healthy Ireland continues to sit on various sub committees including CYPSC Active and Healthy sub-
group, Tusla Child and Family Support Network, and Mental Heath Ireland wellbeing board subgroup. 
 
Healthy Ireland continues to collaborate with Sharon Richardson of the HSE on making Leitrim 
Dementia Friendly through the Understand Together Initiative. The latest event was the inaugural ‘Music 
Café’ which took place in Breffni Family Resource Centre with Charlie McGettigand local musicians 
leading a music circle for people living with dementia, while carers were treated to a session with Inner 
Harmony Health practitioner and nutritional Therapist Laura Fergus who provided coping mechanisms 
and nutritional advice for the carers. 
 
Healthy Ireland presented a summary of results from 2025 to The Age Friendly Alliance.

Community Recognition Fund 
Leitrim has been allocated over €2.2 million under this funding programme, which will be invested 
across 16 capital projects throughout the county. All projects have commenced and two projects now 
completed. 
➢ Allen Gaels GAA Club for which €207,275 was granted for the installation of an Astro Turf pitch  
➢ Lough Rinn Dragon Boating Club New Building and Equipment Expansion project with grant 
aid of €84,000   
 
Local Authority Integration Team (LAIT) 
In December, we initiated the administration of the Irish Refugee Protection Programme (IRPP) by 
recruiting a Resettlement Worker 
 
The Integration Team delivered 11 clinics to assess needs and identify supports for the cohort we work 
with. Three clinics focused on Beneficiaries of Temporary Protection (BOTP), while the remaining eight 
were dedicated to International Protection Accommodation Centres in Leitrim. 
 
Three ‘Offer a Home’ activations were successfully completed in December, securing accommodation for 
three family units. In total, this provided housing for five adults and three children. 
 
The Integration Team collaborated with North Connaught Youth Services to host two sensory-friendly 
Santa events—one in Drumkeerin and the other in Ballinamore. These community integration events 
were open to all families with children who are neurodivergent or have additional needs. In total, 13 
families attended across both events, representing the Irish community, International Protection 
Applicants, and Beneficiaries of Temporary Protection. 
The LAIT collaborated with Leitrim Development Company (LDC) and Leitrim International Community 
Group (LICG) to host the Festival of Nations at the Island Theatre, Ballinamore. This event was a 
celebration of cultural diversity, bringing together communities from across the region. Attendees 
included members of the Irish community, International Protection Applicants, and representatives from 
Ukrainian, Chinese, and Indian communities. To facilitate participation, LAIT funded transport from the 
IPAS Centre in Dromahair and provided on-the-day support to ensure the event’s success.

• Recruitment for the QQI Level 7 is completed. We received 45 applications for 25 places. 
Applications were assessed and successful candidate were notified before the Chrismas break. 
The course is due to start 14th January

• The first meeting on the Environmental & Biodiversity Steering Committee took place on 4th 
December in Drumshanbo. Philip Farrelly Ltd have been contracted to deliver a cross-border 
biodiversity and environmental project also attended the meeting. 
• We are continuing to roll out Digital Camps for young people with the next camp scheduled to 
take place in Kinlough Digital Hub. 
 
Celebrating Cultural Diversity  
• The Leitrim Development Company officially launched their PEACEPUS Traveller Development 
programme in December. 
 
PEACEPLUS Shannonside Peace Arena (1.4) 
• 
Senior management and the SRC committee have had a number of meetings with McAdam 
Design who are finalising designs and QS budget costings for the entire SRC development. 
• 
These should be ready for the next Project Board meeting in January which includes reps from 
funders SEUPB, Dept of Communities, NI and the DRCDG 
 
Local Community Safety Partnership (LCSP) 
• Ministerial approval received for Leitrim LCSP nominations. All members notified of their 
appointment by Minister.  
• Induction of Leitrim Community Safety Partnership Members scheduled for January 27th 2026, 
with inaugural meeting to elect Chairperson to happen the following week.  
• €10,000 set up costs and salary recoupment were received from Dept of Justice. Further 
clarification on future funding of the programme to be received in early 2026.  
• Attendance at Local Community Safety Partnership Engagement Meeting. Additional 
clarifications on National Strategy received with first draft to be completed by April 14th 2026. 
• Supported the roll out of cross county Storm Preparedness Workshops for community members 
delivering information on Health, Personal Safety and Storm Preparedness. Events held in 
Ballinamore and Mohill with a further event to be scheduled for Manorhamilton in Q1 of 2026. 
• Coordination of the development of a public information video on Storm Preparedness to roll out 
on social media channels over Christmas period to provide clear messaging on personal 
responsibility to be prepared for 72 hours ahead of any emergency.  
• Work ongoing on the set up of 10 Community Support Centres across the County to support in the 
event of an emergency.

LIBRARY SERVICES 
December was a very busy month across the library network. Over 9000 visits were made to the libraries 
over the course of the month and there were 125 new members who joined Leitrim library Service in 
December.  
During the month of December, the usual events such as book club and writer group meetings as well as 
craft groups, exercise classes, scrabble, bridge and language sessions took place.  There was good usage 
of the Sensory Room at Mohill Library and Cubbie at Manorhamilton Library.  
Family Time at your Library 
A range of Christmas themed events took place across the library network There was great fun at 
Carrigallen Library's Holly Jolly Christmas Craft event with Julie Smith, who read some lovely Christmas 
stories, including ‘Santa got stuck up the Chimney’. 
Santa dropped into Drumshanbo Library to meet the children from St. Patrick National School and Bo 
Peep Kids. It was a fun morning of stories and singing. 
Carrick Library had both the Senior Infants classes from Scoil Mhuire in for Christmas Storytime with 
Grainne. The Children sang Christmas songs and listened to lots of lovely Christmas stories. 
Kiltyclogher Library had a clay modelling session for the children of Scoil Mhic Diarmada . 
Healthy Ireland 
Health and Well Being Pharmacist, Maj Cunningham, provided a number of insightful discussions on 
women’s health. 
Ciorcal Comhrá/ Irish Language   
Irish Language session continues to attract strong attendance and enthusiasm in Ballinamore, Mohill 
and Dromahair library. 
Digital skills 
Digital skills programs funded under Healthy Leitrim continued to be rolled out across the library 
network, meeting an overwhelmingly high demand.  
Local Studies 
Mary Conefrey and Sarah Garden visited TY History Students in Manorhamilton and Carrigallen and 
made a presentation to students and History teachers re Young Historian Award 2026 
Local Historian Padraig Griffin presented a talk in Ballinamore Library on Thursday December 11th 
entitled ‘Church – State relations in Ireland since 1800’ was well attended. The talk looked at how the 
Influential Roman Catholic Church maintained relations with the State both before and after the Anglo-
Irish Treaty and the setting up of the independent Irish State in 1922.

ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT, REGENERATION, SUSTAINABLE 
TRANSPORT & EMERGENCY SERVICES 
ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT 
STEM Passport for Inclusion- Maynooth University & ATU 
3 Secondary Schools, Lough Allen College, Drumshanbo Vocational School and Mohill Community 
college had the second one day workshop of STEM Passport for Inclusion programme (level 6 award) 
during the month of December. TY students from Carrigallen Vocational School will commence the 
programme in January 2026. A number of National Schools around the County have signed up to take 
part in the Microsoft Dreamspace Programme 2025/2026. 
 
Carrick on Shannon Community CCTV Scheme Extension 
Approval was received from The Garda Commissioner in December for an extension of the Community 
CCTV Scheme in Carrick on Shannon, adding a further 25 cameras at 12 additional locations in Carrick on 
Shannon including the new boardwalk, the riverside and the new carpark to the rear of main street. 
 
Carrick on Shannon Business Campus 
The tender for consultancy services in relation to the proposed Enterprise Hub at Carrick on Shannon 
Business Campus closed on 15th December, with three tenders received.  This body of work involves the 
development a suite of work packages to move the project from concept validation to implementation 
readiness, through the development of a comprehensive business, design and governance framework.  
The tender will be evaluated on 9th January.   
 
County Promotion 
The “50 Miles in January” Challenge was officially launched at Carrick Business Campus on December 
3rd. This initiative, delivered in partnership with Leitrim GAA and LGFA, is expected to enjoy strong 
community support once again. As part of its commitment, Leitrim County Council has funded a series of 
ambassador videos to promote the campaign while aligning with key council objectives. In addition, 
consistent with previous years, the council has provided sponsorship to Leitrim GAA and LGFA to help 
drive the success of this popular initiative. 
 
Leitrim Diaspora 
Progress continued on developing the framework for the Leitrim Diaspora Strategy 2026–2030. On 16th 
December, Leitrim County Council met with representatives from the Department of Foreign Affairs’ Irish 
Abroad Unit, where the department provided an update on the development of the national diaspora 
strategy. 
 
Leitrim Economic Forum and Global Business Network 
A meeting of the Leitrim Economic Forum took place on 5th December; the next meeting of the group is 
scheduled for 6th February 2026.  A meeting of the Leitrim Global Business Network took place on 10th 
December; the next meeting of the group is scheduled for 24th February 2026. Work is ongoing on the 
procurement of a consultant to deliver a new Economic and Skills Strategy for County Leitrim, it is 
anticipated that work will commence early in 2026.  Discussions are taking place on planning a Leitrim 
Business/Ambassadors Summit for 2026. A meeting of the working group for the Leitrim 
Business/Ambassadors summit is scheduled to take place on 12th January 2026. 
 
DRCD Funded Schemes 
Funding announcements under the Town and Village Main Scheme and Project Development Measures 
were made in December. A total of €26 million was allocated to 116 projects nationwide, with Leitrim

12 
 
receiving a total of 4 projects amounting to €966,801. The 3 projects funded under the Main Scheme 
include phase 2 redevelopment works to the former Garda Barracks Keshcarrigan - €500,000, 
enhancement of the public realm at The Dock, Carrick on Shannon - €300,000 and Streetscape 
Enhancement Scheme for Carrigallen - €139,705. The Project Development Measure project funded was 
for the redevelopment and extension of the Fenagh Visitor Centre - €27,096.  
 
TOURISM 
Fáilte Ireland DEDP 
An in-person meeting of the Fáilte Ireland Destination and Experience Development Plan (DEDP) was 
held at the Arigna Mining Centre. Representatives from each county participated in a detailed review of 
the plan’s priorities and actions. Fáilte Ireland also presented updates on several ongoing projects 
aligned with the DEDP, including initiatives to enhance visitor experiences, strengthen regional 
branding, and support sustainable tourism development. 
NPA 
The Tourism Team, in collaboration with the Northwest Regional Assembly, is actively exploring the 
scope of a potential project for submission under the new Northern Periphery and Arctic (NPA) 
programme call in February. Discussions are underway with potential partners to ensure a strong 
consortium and a competitive application. 
Festival & Event Grants 
All claims for the 2025 Festival and Event Grants have now been processed. These grants have played a 
key role in sustaining community led events and attracting visitors to the county. Looking ahead, 
planning has commenced for the development of a new scheme to be introduced in 2026. 
Budget Preparation 
Budget and marketing plans for the upcoming year have been prepared to support tourism initiatives. 
This includes allocating resources for promotional campaigns, digital marketing, and experience 
development. The plans also prioritise investment in collaborative projects with regional partners, 
ensuring that Leitrim’s tourism offering is effectively positioned within the regional and national tourism 
landscape. 
Social Media Engagement 
Throughout December, the Tourism Team maintained active engagement across Instagram, Facebook, 
and Twitter, sharing seasonal content and promoting local attractions. This activity was strengthened by 
the countywide photography competition held earlier in the year, with winning entries featured 
prominently in the Leitrim Calendar. The calendar was distributed through libraries, council offices, and 
to members of the overseas diaspora, where it has been warmly received. Feedback highlighted its role 
in fostering community pride and maintaining connections with Leitrim abroad. The campaign also 
helped grow online audiences, increase post reach, and encourage user-generated content that 
showcases the county’s natural beauty and cultural heritage. 
 
LOCAL ENTERPRISE OFFICE (LEO) 
Training, Mentoring & Export      
A number of people received training in December as we ran a series of courses such as AI Training; 
Business Advice Clinic; Women in Business Event in Longford Arms Hotel. Demand for one-to-one 
mentoring continues to remain high. Assistance is also available on Export related issues and can be 
booked online free of charge to discuss any issues facing businesses or identifying and managing 
opportunities available for exporting.

13 
 
All In A Days Work Programmes & Associated Financial Supports 
The “All In A Days Work” campaign continues to be rolled out on the areas of Lean, Green and Digital 
supports.  There is significant growth in demand for all three supports, in particular the Energy Efficiency 
Grant (EEG) and Grow Digital (GD) Voucher. The EEG, with up to 75% of eligible costs up to a maximum 
grant of €10,000 can be supported following the completion of a Green for Business, Green Start or a 
SEAI Energy Audit. The GD voucher is a grant covering 50% of eligible costs (minimum grant of €500 up to 
a maximum grant of €5,000) limited to new software subscriptions for a period of 12 and training and 
configuration of the software. 
Atlantic Economic Corridor Update:  
Interreg Europe Digital Rural 
Leitrim continues its partnership under Interreg Europe. The Digital Rural Project empowers rural 
communities through smart technologies and collaborative policymaking to foster sustainable regional 
development.  
 
PEACE Plus – DS3 Project 
The DS3 Project under PEACE Plus (Smart Towns & Villages) launched in November 2025, running until 
July 2028. It promotes cross-border collaboration through ICT in community services and economic 
activity. Leitrim County Council leads Work Package 2 to lead out a mobile fab lab. Workshops are due to 
commence in February.  
 
Creative Heartlands 
The programme ‘Creative Heartlands on Screen’ continues with training and mentoring for the screen 
sector in Leitrim, Sligo and Roscommon with funding from Screen Ireland. Training and networking 
events commenced in October and will run until May 2026. A comprehensive mentorship programme 
will be established.  
 
Northwest Regional Enterprise Plan Implementation 
Northwest Vision Development 
The three Chief Executives from Leitrim/Sligo/Donegal are collaborating to develop a Northwest Region 
Vision which will feed into the REP development in 2026. In December the three Chief Executives met to 
review OCO’s progress and to provide guidance.  
Energy Working Group 
A multi-agency supported project is underway which will explore the opportunities available to the 
region with available unused energy from our renewable energy sources in the region e.g. onshore wind 
energy. Opportunities being explored are green energy parks, marketing, hydrogen etc.  
10xNW 2026 
Following a very successful event in 2025, a collaborative course of multiple agencies in the Northwest 
region are coming together to host the 10xNW entrepreneurship exchange in February 2026 in Leitrim. The 
working group have convened and are planning this.  
Next REP development 
The final report of the Northwest Regional Enterprise Plan 2022-2025 is currently in draft form and once 
approved by DETE will be published on DETE website. Currently DETE are undergoing a review of the REP’s 
with the intention of taking recommendations from the review towards the next REP development which 
is due to kick off Q1 2026.

CAPITAL PROJECTS 
Carrick on Shannon Flood Relief Scheme  
The project team are currently progressing environmental assessments required to support a planning 
application for the scheme.  A workshop focused on enhancing the environment where possible whilst 
also achieving robust flood protection was held which was attended by members of various 
departments in Leitrim and Roscommon County Councils, OPW, NMS and the Local Authorities Waters 
Programme (LAWPRO). A design freeze has been achieved having identified a preferred scheme.  
Archaeology Slit trenching in the surrounds of the old castle are scheduled are complete, and the 
Environmental Impact Assessment (EIAR) is nearing completion. Full details of the project are available 
on the project website: www.carrickonshannonfrs.ie. 
 
Leitrim Village Flood Relief Scheme

15 
 
A design freeze has been achieved having identified a preferred scheme.  Archaeology Slit trenching in 
the surrounds of the old castle are scheduled are complete, and the Environmental Impact Assessment 
(EIAR) is well underway. An additional workshop was held with Ryan Hanley, LCC and OPW, to discuss 
the cost benefit of the scheme and a potential business case to progress the project to planning and 
detailed design. Full details of the project are available on the project website Full details of the project 
are available on website www.leitrimvillagefrs.ie` 
 
Mohill Flood Relief Scheme  
The hydraulic analysis and economic feasibility on this project to determine the need/extent for flood 
defences have been substantially complete in Mohill by OPW in partnership with LCC Capital Projects 
Office. We await OPW’s determination, following a business case submitted to them in September 2024.  
 
OPW Minor Flood Schemes 
Dromahair Scheme  
The Capital Projects Team received planning consent from An Coimisiún Pleanála in Q2 of 2025. We are 
currently drafting land owner agreements. We plan to go to tender in March 2026 to assess the most 
economically advantageous tender. Following this, we will seek approval from the OPW to proceed with 
the construction of the scheme in June 2026. 
 
Leitrim Village (Keadue Road Scheme) Scheme  
This minor works scheme is substantially complete, with some outstanding accommodation works in 
the adjacent Drumhierny Housing Estate. 
 
Manorhamilton Minor Works Scheme  
This minor works scheme is substantially complete with a claim for funding to be complete. 
 
Carrick on Shannon Urban Regeneration Scheme 
We are awaiting thermal imaging to facilitate the repair of the damaged handrails. Contact has been 
made with DHB regarding defects identified in some of the lighting. 
 
Manorhamilton Public Realm Scheme 
Contract No 1 for public realm works on Main Street has been completed. A contractor has been 
appointed to complete Contract No 2 for works at Enterprise lands. Works will commence in Q1 2026. 
 
Mohill Public Realm Scheme  
Works have been completed. A Substantial Completion Certificate has been issued to the Contractor. 
Outstanding snags to be completed. 
 
Drumshanbo ExChange.  
Tenders for the works contract have now been returned and a report on tenders prepared. It is expected 
that a contractor will be appointed later in Q1 2026 subject to Department approval and available 
budget. 
 
Carrick Business Campus 
DHB Architects have completed the detailed design and tender documents for the current project. The 
Tender Documents and Bill of Quantities (BOQ) are divided into two elements: 
• 
Element 1: Fit-out of the ground floor of Phase 2, including a full mechanical and electrical 
upgrade and installation.

16 
 
• 
Element 2: Energy reduction works (fabric upgrade) for the ground and first floors of Phase 2, 
along with completion of mechanical and electrical works to shell and core standard.  
 
Additional funding is required to proceed with the upgrade proposals, as only partial funding has been 
received from SEAI and RRDF. An application for increased funding is currently with the RRDF, and we 
await their decision 
 
Drumshanbo Food Innovation & Knowledge Hub   
Collins Boyd Engineers and Architects have been appointed as designers, ER and PSDP. They are 
currently developing the detailed design for the scheme. 
 
Shannonside Recreational Campus 
Pre-qualification tenders have been received and are currently being assessed. The final design is being 
prepared, with the full tender scheduled for publication in Q1.  
 
Carrick Arts and Community Centre (Colemans Building along Main Street) 
Works commenced in October and are progressing steadily. Handover is expected before Q3 2026. 
 
Manorhamilton NCYS Building   
Works are substantially completed with only snagging outstanding. Building to be handed over in Q1. 
 
Leitrim Village Community Facility  
A planning application for the scheme was submitted in December 2025 by the Leitrim Village 
Development Group and we await a decision. 
 
SLNCR Greenway – Sligo to Enniskillen  
Funding is now in place via Shared Island fund and DFI for service contracts & PLO services in 
Fermanagh. Phase 2 (Deliverables & Reports) are now complete. Phase 3 (Design & Environmental) has 
commenced. Surveys are being undertaken at present and the Design Team are now working on 
optioneering the best fit route within the Preferred Corridor. 
 
Carrick on Shannon to Battlebridge Blueway   
The consultants are required to carry out additional aquatic surveys in accordance with the IFI scoping 
response and the opinion from An Coimisiún Pleanála submission. They are also progressing the EIAR 
with the intention of lodging a planning application to An Coimisiún Pleanála by the end of November 
2026.  
 
South Leitrim Greenway  
The Project Outline Document has been updated for the TII and we are awaiting TII approval to 
commence Phase 1 (Concept & Feasibility) and appoint a Consultant Engineer for Phases 1 to 4 inclusive. 
 
Hartley Bridge 
Following planning approval from An Bord Pleanála in December 2023, funding has been received from 
the Department of Transport to advance this project. Punch Consulting Engineers have been appointed 
the detailed design and tender documents were completed in Q4 2025.   
 
Dromod Roosky Greyway  
Funding was approved by the Department of Rural and Community Development and the Gaeltacht in 
the amount of €500,000 in Dec 2025. Tender Documents for the scheme are currently being prepared.

17 
 
 
Acres Lake Facility Centre 
The contractor is currently completing the snagging of the building and we await certification of the 
works. It is be expected that the facility will be open to the public in Q1 2026.  
 
Narrow Gauge Trail Drumshanbo 
The trail is completed and open to the public with a couple of minor snagging works to be completed. 
 
Fenagh Abbey Trail 
A geo physical Survey has now been completed on site.  It is expected that the scheme will be submitted
